answer: After sunset the light fades along a smooth curve whose slope depends on latitude, season and cloud. A light sensor logs lux through twilight, and the verifier fits the decay slope against the expected curve, so a hill mapped in an atlas, a garden terrace and a plain open to the zenith each fade at a different rate. A farm switching lamps on and off cannot reproduce the smooth natural slope, and one recorded dusk reused across accounts is instantly identical.
